<r>℣.</r> Iube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
<r>1 Reg 9:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> Cum autem veníssent in terram Suph, dixit Saul ad púerum, qui erat cum eo: Veni et revertámur, ne forte dimíserit pater meus ásinas et sollícitus sit pro nobis.
<n>6</n> Qui ait ei: Ecce vir Dei est in civitáte hac, vir nóbilis: omne quod lóquitur, sine ambiguitáte venit; nunc ergo eámus illuc, si forte índicet nobis de via nostra, propter quam vénimus.
<n>7</n> Dixítque Saul ad púerum suum: Ecce íbimus: quid ferémus ad virum Dei? panis defécit in sitárciis nostris, et spórtulam non habémus, ut demus hómini Dei, nec quidquam áliud.
<n>8</n> Rursum puer respóndit Sauli et ait: Ecce invénta est in manu mea quarta pars statéris argénti: demus hómini Dei, ut índicet nobis viam nostram.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli:
* Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.
<r>℣.</r> Convertímini ad eum in toto corde vestro, et auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri.
<r>℟.</r> Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
<r>1 Sam 9:5-8</r>
<n>5</n> And when they were come to the land of Suph, Saul said to the servant that was with him: Come, let us return, lest perhaps my father forget the asses, and be concerned for us.
<n>6</n> And he said to him: Behold there is a man of God in this city, a famous man: all that he saith, cometh certainly to pass. Now therefore let us go thither, perhaps he may tell us of our way, for which we are come.
<n>7</n> And Saul said to his servant: Behold we will go: but what shall we carry to the man of God? the bread is spent in our bags: and we have no present to make to the man of God, nor any thing at all.
<n>8</n> The servant answered Saul again, and said: Behold there is found in my hand the fourth part of a sicle of silver, let us give it to the man of God, that he may tell us our way.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve Him Only
* And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.
<r>℣.</r> Return unto Him with all your hearts, and put away the strange gods from among you.
<r>℟.</r> And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>1 Reg 9:10-13</r>
<n>10</n> Et dixit Saul ad púerum suum: Optimus sermo tuus. Veni, eámus. Et iérunt in civitátem in qua erat vir Dei.
<n>11</n> Cumque ascénderent clivum civitátis, invenérunt puéllas egrediéntes ad hauriéndam aquam, et dixérunt eis: Num hic est Videns?
<n>12</n> Quæ respondéntes, dixérunt illis: Hic est: ecce ante te, festína nunc: hódie enim venit in civitátem, quia sacrifícium est hódie pópuli in excélso.
<n>13</n> Ingrediéntes urbem, statim inveniétis eum ántequam ascéndat excélsum ad vescéndum, neque enim comesúrus est pópulus donec ille véniat: quia ipse benedícit hóstiæ, et deínceps cómedunt qui vocáti sunt. Nunc ergo conscéndite, quia hódie reperiétis eum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Percússit Saul mille, et David decem míllia:
quia manus Dómini erat cum illo: percússit Philisthǽum,
* Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Nonne iste est David, de quo canébant in choro, dicéntes: Saul percússit mille, et David decem míllia in míllibus suis?
<r>℟.</r> Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<r>1 Reg 9:14-17</r>
<n>14</n> Et ascendérunt in civitátem. Cumque illi ambulárent in médio urbis, appáruit Sámuel egrédiens óbviam eis, ut ascénderet in excélsum.
<n>15</n> Dóminus autem reveláverat aurículam Samuélis, ante unam diem quam veníret Saul, dicens:
<n>16</n> Hac ipsa hora, quæ nunc est, cras mittam virum ad te de terra Béniamin, et unges eum ducem super pópulum meum Israël, et salvábit pópulum meum de manu Philisthinórum, quia respéxi pópulum meum; venit enim clamor eórum ad me.
<n>17</n> Cumque aspexísset Sámuel Saulem Dóminus dixit ei: Ecce vir, quem díxeram tibi: iste dominábitur pópulo meo.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Montes Gélboë, nec ros nec plúvia véniant super vos,
* Ubi cecidérunt fortes Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Omnes montes, qui estis in circúitu eius, vísitet Dóminus: a Gélboë autem tránseat.
<r>℟.</r> Ubi cecidérunt fortes Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Fortes Israël.

<r>1 Sam 9:14-17</r>
<n>14</n> And they went up into the city. And when they were walking in the midst of the city, behold Samuel was coming out over against them, to go up to the high place.
<n>15</n> Now the Lord had revealed to the ear of Samuel the day before Saul came, saying:
<n>16</n> Tomorrow about this same hour I will send thee a man of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be ruler over my people Israel: and he shall save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked down upon my people, because their cry is come to me.

<r>℟.</r> For there are the mighty of Israel fallen.

<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.

b.2ff459ebd0:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Idus Iúnii Luna quinta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>N</h>oménti, in Sabínis, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Primi et Feliciáni fratrum, sub Diocletiáno et Maximiáno Imperatóribus. Hi gloriósi Mártyres, cum longǽvam in Dómino vitam duxíssent, et nunc simul pária, nunc singillátim divérsa et exquisíta pertulíssent torménta, ambo tandem felícis pugnæ cursum, a Nomentáno Prǽside Promóto animadvérsi gládio, consummavérunt. Ipsórum autem Mártyrum córpora, póstea Romam transláta, in Ecclésia sancti Stéphani Protomártyris, in monte Cǽlio, honorífice collocáta sunt.
<h>A</h>génni, in Gállia, pássio sancti Vincéntii, Levítæ et Mártyris, qui, ob Christi fidem, verbéribus diríssime cæsus et gládio decollátus est.
<h>A</h>pud Antiochíam sanctæ Pelágiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quam sancti Ambrósius et Ioánnes Chrysostómus magnis éfferunt láudibus.
<h>S</h>yracúsis, in Sicília, sancti Maximiáni Epíscopi, cuius sanctus Gregórius Papa sǽpius méminit.
<h>A</h>ndriæ, in Apúlia, sancti Richárdi, qui fuit primus eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, et miráculis cláruit.
<h>I</h>n Ióna, Scótiæ ínsula, sancti Colúmbæ, Presbýteri et Abbátis.
<h>E</h>déssæ, in Sýria, sancti Iuliáni Mónachi, cuius præclára gesta sanctus Ephræm Diáconus scripsit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.a293f23d09:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 9th 2027, the 5th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>U</h>pon the Celian Mount of Rome, the holy Martyrs Primus and Felician, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian. These glorious martyrs had led a long life together, and had suffered diverse and dreadful torments sometimes together, and sometimes apart. At length they brought their happy fight to a close, being beheaded under Promotus, President of Mentana.
<h>A</h>t Agen, in Gaul, [in the third century,] suffered the holy martyr Vincent the Levite.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, [in the year 304,] the holy Virgin martyr Pelagia, whom holy Ambrose and John Chrysostom do greatly praise.
<h>A</h>t Syracuse, [in the year 594,] holy Maximian, Bishop [of that see,] of whom holy Pope Gregory the Great doth oftentimes make mention.
<h>A</h>t Andria, in Apulia, [in the twelfth century,] holy Richard, the first Bishop of that city, famous for wondrous works.
<h>I</h>n Scotland, [in the year 597,] holy Colum, Priest and Confessor, [founder and first Abbot of Iona.]
<h>A</h>t Edessa, in Syria, [in the fourth century,] the holy monk Julian, whose illustrious acts are written by the holy Deacon Ephraim.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
